subject: [PATCH v7 1/6] fuse: decouple fuse_ring creation from ent registration

reviews.author: Baokun Li
reviews.summary:
reviewer noted that the patch does not handle the case where FUSE_INIT reply processing fails and requested a check to be added to ensure the ring is properly cleaned up in this scenario

Reviewer Baokun Li expressed concern that enabling io-uring without FUSE_OVER_IO_URING allows a capability beyond what was negotiated, and suggested printing the negotiated flags to dmesg at INIT time for easier issue detection.

Reviewer noted that clearing fch->io_uring on REGISTER failure may reject subsequent io_uring commands with -EOPNOTSUPP while the data path is still running on uring ops, and suggested that fch->io_uring should remain set even after a single REGISTER failure.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi all,

On 2026/8/20 04:05, Bernd Schubert wrote:

---

I share Bernd's concern here. Allowing io-uring without
FUSE_OVER_IO_URING means enabling a capability beyond what was
negotiated. We should honor the negotiated feature set, and print
the negotiated flags to dmesg at INIT time so issues like this are
easy to spot.

---

BTW, the current code clears fch->io_uring on REGISTER failure:

        if (err) {
            fch->io_uring = 0;
            wake_up_all(&fch->blocked_waitq);
            return err;
        }

But by then other entries may have already registered successfully,
fiq->ops is switched to fuse_io_uring_ops, and requests are flowing
through the uring path. Clearing fch->io_uring here may reject all
subsequent io_uring commands with -EOPNOTSUPP while the data path
is still running on uring ops.

fch->io_uring is a protocol fact \u2014 the daemon negotiated
FUSE_OVER_IO_URING at INIT time. A single REGISTER failure should
not regress it, at least not once the ring is ready. The daemon
can retry; the negotiated capability should be permanent.


Thanks,
Baokun

reviews.author: Joanne Koong (author)
reviews.summary:
Author acknowledged that changing the existing behavior would break backwards compatibility and cited a specific kernel version (6.14) as evidence.

Author addressed a concern that the check in fuse_uring_cmd() would allow enabling IO_URING even if admin disabled it, explaining that the check is an && not an || and will only return -EOPNOTSUPP if admin disables enable_uring.
reviews.raw_body:
Not sure if you missed this reply [1], but will copy and paste it here:

This is pre-existing behavior that's been there since the beginning
(kernel version 6.14). I don't think we can change this now, or
it'll break backwards compatibility, like Miklos's loraw program.

---

This is also pre-existing behavior. The check in fuse_uring_cmd() is a
&& not an ||. It'll only return -EOPNOTSUPP if admin disables
enable_uring.

Thanks,
Joanne

[1] https://lore.kernel.org/fuse-devel/CAJnrk1Z_ioW02xbrUekpzSJNerHL=XH-VYqHmUXFzyUD4HDNdQ@mail.gmail.com/

reviews.author: Bernd Schubert
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that the current implementation may lead to a deadlock due to incorrect lock ordering, and also allows for module option bypass and flag bypass between fuse-server and kernel, suggesting switching to FUSE_OVER_IO_URING2 flag instead.
reviews.raw_body:
I think we need to discuss this. I had replied that the current
accidental scheme we

- deadlock (lock order), with bg_lock being one issue, but I bet there
is more
- module option bypass
- bypass of what fuse-client/kernel announces

I.e. if a fuse-server did implement the accidental scheme, it was broken
anyway.

If wanted to be paranoid, we would switch to FUSE_OVER_IO_URING2 flag
and ignore FUSE_OVER_IO_URING. I hope you don't insist on allowing
fuse-server to set flags that fuse-server doesn't even announce...

Thanks,
Bernd

reviews.author: Joanne Koong (author)
reviews.summary:
Author pushed back on the suggestion to introduce a new flag (FUSE_OVER_IO_URING2) to handle servers using older versions of libfuse, arguing that it would be behaviorally identical to just enforcing FUSE_OVER_IO_URING and could break compatibility

Author pushed back on feedback about potential backwards compatibility issues, suggesting that the decision should be left up to Miklos. She also proposed a potential fix for a lockdep issue by restructuring the flush_bg_queue() function.
reviews.raw_body:
I don't think a new FUSE_OVER_IO_URING2 flag helps. If the kernel
ignores FUSE_OVER_IO_URING as you describe, servers using older
versions of libfuse will break. If it accepts both flags, it's
behaviorally identical to just enforcing FUSE_OVER_IO_URING.

---

I think this is a call better left up to Miklos. I don't know how
rigorously it is enforced in linux that nothing should break backwards
compatibility. The code was released in March 2025 as part of kernel
version 6.14, so it's been roughly a year and a half, which I guess
isn't that long in the grand scheme of things, but if Miklos has his
loraw server program that relies on this, it's probably likely there's
other users out there who have servers that would similarly just break
if we switch the policy now.

I haven't had time to look deeply at the lockdep thing you wrote
about, but from a first glance, couldn't we fix it at the source?
flush_bg_queue() calls ->send_req() while holding the fch->bg_lock
which is what creates the bg_lock -> queue->lock deadlock. If it
instead only does the background accounting under the lock and moves
the requests to a caller-provided list where the caller only sends
*after* dropping the bg_lock, doesn't that solve the deadlock? This
would fix it for every server regardless of whether it sent
FUSE_OVER_IO_URING or not. I'll try to get some time to look at this
next week.

Thanks,
Joanne

reviews.author: Bernd Schubert
reviews.summary:
The reviewer objects to the introduction of an unannounced flag for io_uring_enabled, considering it a behavioral change that should be debated.

Reviewer Bernd Schubert expressed concern that the patch may introduce new issues due to runtime switching, and suggested discussing further before proceeding.
reviews.raw_body:
Well, setting a flag that is not announced by kernel is not ok
either. Yes, it is change in behavior, but it is debatable.

---

I have a basic patch for that, but I fear testing will bring up ore
issues when we switch at run time.

Let's discuss in a few min.


Thanks,
Bernd

2026-08-20.patch_summary: This patch decouples the creation of fuse_ring from entry registration in the FUSE (Filesystem in Userspace) driver. Currently, the ring is created lazily on the first FUSE_IO_URING_CMD_REGISTER command, which can lead to concurrent creations and requires open-coded handling. The patch moves the ring creation to the FUSE_INIT reply processing after a server has negotiated and set FUSE_OVER_IO_URING, ensuring that the ring is published before the connection is marked initialized. This change simplifies the code and reduces the risk of concurrent creations.

reviews.author: Baokun Li
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Baokun Li expressed concern that enabling capabilities beyond what was negotiated can introduce inconsistencies, referencing issues found in their downstream tree related to the fch->io_uring switch.

Reviewer Baokun Li noted that the current implementation of io_uring flags has unclear boundaries and inconsistent states, specifically mentioning enable_uring, fch->io_uring, and ring->ready. He suggested a clean design where fch->io_uring is set at INIT time based on negotiated flags and user-controlled enable_uring, and then write-once, with the io_uring path taken when ring->ready and falling back to classic /dev/fuse otherwise.
reviews.raw_body:
Yes, I saw it, but pre-existing doesn't necessarily mean correct.
Enabling capabilities beyond what was negotiated easily introduces
inconsistencies.

In our recent hardening work we found that the fch->io_uring switch
causes anomalies in several mechanisms (mostly in our downstream tree),
which is why I replied in Bernd's thread \u2014 he raised the
enable_uring / fch->io_uring bypass there.

---

Yes, that's exactly the problem. Right now we have several flags
with unclear boundaries:

 enable_uring: user-controlled, can be toggled at any time
 fch->io_uring: set to 1 at INIT negotiation, but cleared to 0
   on any entry registration failure \u2014 even if other entries
   have already registered successfully and fiq->ops has been
   switched to uring ops. The two states are inconsistent.
 ring->ready: set when at least one entry has registered

I think the clean design would be: at INIT time, decide based on
enable_uring and the negotiated flags whether to initialize uring
and set fch->io_uring. After that, enable_uring is no longer
consulted \u2014 fch->io_uring is write-once. When ring->ready (at
least one entry registered), take the io_uring path; otherwise
fall back to the classic /dev/fuse path. This way each
variable has a single, clear semantic.


Thanks,
Baokun

reviews.author: Baokun Li
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that a server skipping FUSE_OVER_IO_URING was never in a well-defined state due to lack of blocking guarantee and lock ordering protection, and agreed with the patch's decoupling approach.
reviews.raw_body:
Agreed. A server that skips FUSE_OVER_IO_URING was never in a
well-defined state \u2014 no blocking guarantee, no lock ordering
protection, nothing. There is nothing to preserve compatibility
with.


Thanks,
Baokun

reviews.author: Baokun Li
reviews.summary: The reviewer agrees that decoupling fuse_ring creation from ent registration is a good approach, as it simplifies the code structure by eliminating nested operations.
reviews.raw_body:
Makes sense \u2014 separating dequeue from send eliminates the nesting
structurally.


Cheers,
Baokun

2026-08-21.patch_summary: This patch decouples the creation of fuse_ring from entry registration in the FUSE (Filesystem in Userspace) driver. Currently, the ring is created lazily on the first FUSE_IO_URING_CMD_REGISTER command, which can lead to concurrent creations and requires open-coded handling. The patch moves the ring creation to the FUSE_INIT reply processing after a server has negotiated and set FUSE_OVER_IO_URING, ensuring that the ring is published before the connection is marked initialized. This change simplifies the code and reduces the risk of concurrent creations.
